newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the fourth-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data, dealer said on Friday.

They said the market is also waiting for possible direction from today's release of the U.S. January Chicago purchasing managers index (PMI) figures, December new home sales and the University of Michigan consumer confidence index data.
GDP figures for the fourth-quarter are forecast to have risen at a 3.9 percent growth rate compared with a 2.1 percent growth rate reported in the third quarter.
The January Chicago PMI is expected to be unchanged from December's 57.4 percent.
New homes sales for December are expected to be around 745,000 units compared with 772,000 units reported in November.
The January University of Michigan consumer confidence index is expected to slip to 96.4 percent from December's 96.9 percent.
"Rates were steady to slightly higher in the morning on some weekend booksquaring and ahead of today's fourth-quarter GDP figures," a local dealer said.
"The market is also waiting for tonight's release of the Chicago PMI, new homes sales and University of Michigan consumer confidence index figures," he said.

"I don't think there will be much impact except for the GDP figures, as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he added.
In day-to-day rates, weekend rose 1/8 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, nine-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
